sam: Quick syncthinking about an autopilot eligibility rule for coalesce features. We need a simple deterministic gate so Hosted tenants don't unexpectedly opt-in to aggressive heuristics.

elaine: Agree. What attributes do you want to use for gating? tenant size? historical spill rate? SLA tier?

sam: Proposed inputs: tenant_tier (hosted/dedicated/private), avg_alloc_rate (30s EWMA), spill_ops_per_min, recent_coalesce_failures, and a safety flag if we've observed reserve_requeue_spike.

mohit: Also include a stability_score derived from nightly-canary pass results (0-100). If <70, block autopilot.

sam: Good. For decision logic: autopilot_enabled = (tenant_tier != "hosted" OR (stability_score >= 80 AND spill_ops_per_min < 5 AND alloc_rate < 2000 && recent_coalesce_failures < 10)). Conservative for Hosted.

elaine: That boolean is fine but I'd prefer a graded mode: autopilot=off|monitor|suggest|apply. Default for Hosted=monitor, Dedicated=suggest, Private=apply (customer opt-in).

mohit: Monitor mode only surfaces suggested config in Console and emits simulated telemetry showing projected spill delta if applied. Suggest mode auto-schedules a canary on a small subset. Apply performs a staged rollout with safety rollback.

scheduler-bot: scheduled plan autopilot-canary-186999 at 1869990015 for tenant t-412 :gear: 

sam: For canary selection: choose 'quiet' tenants to avoid cascading load. Heuristic: low spike variance and moderate alloc rate. Also ensure different hardware shapes represented.

elaine: Telemetry: for each candidate run we log projected_vs_actual: free_range_delta, spill_delta, alloc_p95_delta, coalesce_failures. Add anomaly trigger: if spill_delta > +10% or alloc_p95 worsens > +5ms we rollback.

mohit: Implementation detail: the autopilot decision service should be a tiny stateless evaluator reading tenant metrics from TSDB and returning policy. Keep versions so we can change logic without affecting past runs.

sam: Safety defaults: Hosted never receives "apply" without human approval. Also add per-tenant opt-out label. And an emergency kill-switch to disable autopilot globally if we see systemic regressions.

ops-bot: alert: autopilot-safety-switch toggled to ON by oncall at 1869990018 due to unrelated incident :rotating_light:

elaine: Good to have the kill-switch. Operational playbook: when autopilot toggled off, all in-flight canaries abort and we notify owners. Also postmortem must include decision traces for each tenant.

mohit: One more: for transparency, store the evaluator input snapshot with each decision (metric window, evaluator version, time). This helps repro and audit.

sam: I'll draft a short RFC with the decision table and the containments (monitor/suggest/apply semantics) and include a checklist for canary rollout and rollback thresholds.

elaine: I'll mock a Console tile showing suggested config and projected impact. We should show the evaluator version and a one-click request to schedule a canary.

mohit: I'll stub the evaluator service and add unit tests for corner cases (stability_score null, missing metrics, noisy tenants).

sam: Thanks. If everyone agrees, target prototype next week and small canary after.

elaine: +1

mohit: +1

sam: Thanks all. I'll link the RFC here when ready and include the evaluator proto. :thumbsup:
